## SpaceX — Key Facts

---

### Founding & Structure
- Full name: Space Exploration Technologies Corporation
- Founded: March 14, 2002, by Elon Musk
- Headquarters: Starbase, Texas
- Employees (2026): ~22,000
- Mission: Revolutionize space transportation and make humanity multiplanetary

### IPO & Valuation
- SpaceX went public on June 12, 2026 — the largest IPO in history
- Raised $86 billion; shares debuted at $135
- Company valued at approximately $1.8 trillion at IPO
- In early 2026, SpaceX acquired xAI (which runs the Grok AI model and the X social network) from Elon Musk

### Key Firsts & Achievements
- First privately-developed spacecraft to reach Earth orbit
- First commercial spacecraft to dock with the International Space Station (ISS)
- First company to successfully land and reuse orbital-class rocket boosters (Falcon 9)
- Launched NASA astronauts to ISS via Crew Dragon capsule
- Operates Starlink — the world's largest satellite internet constellation (thousands of satellites in low Earth orbit)

### Rocket Fleet
- **Falcon 9**: Workhorse reusable two-stage rocket; primary launch vehicle
- **Falcon Heavy**: Three-core heavy-lift vehicle, one of the most powerful operational rockets
- **Starship**: Fully reusable super-heavy lift rocket system; largest rocket ever built

### Starship Program
- Conducted 5 Starship flight tests in 2025; first 3 failed, final 2 (August & October) were successes
- As of 2026, SpaceX plans to ramp to 25 Starship missions per year, targeting 100/year in subsequent years
- Key 2026 objectives include first orbital propellant transfer (refueling in orbit) and inaugural Florida launch
- Starship selected by NASA under the Artemis program to land astronauts on the Moon
- Elon Musk has stated a ~50/50 probability of an uncrewed Starship Mars attempt in 2026

### Starlink
- Provides broadband internet globally via low Earth orbit satellites
- Tens of thousands of satellites planned in the full constellation
- Used commercially, by governments, and in conflict zones (e.g., Ukraine)

### Business Model
- Revenue from government launch contracts (NASA, U.S. Space Force), commercial satellite launches, and Starlink subscriptions
- Reusability of Falcon 9 boosters dramatically reduces per-launch costs compared to competitors
